title: Complex numbers: Cartesian and polar form
description: The imaginary unit, the complex plane, modulus and argument, and multiplication as rotation plus scaling.

title: Euler's formula
description: e^{i theta} = cos theta + i sin theta derived from Taylor series; complex exponentials as rotating points.

title: Roots of unity and complex eigenvalues of rotations
description: The n-th roots of unity as vertices of a regular polygon, their sum, and rotation matrices having eigenvalues e^{+-i theta}.

title: Discrete Fourier transform and the FFT
description: The DFT as a change of basis to the roots-of-unity basis, its derivation, inverse, and the divide-and-conquer FFT.

title: Frequency resolution, aliasing and Nyquist
description: Bin spacing fs/N, why sampling below twice the highest frequency folds frequencies, and leakage.

title: Convolution theorem and spectrograms
description: Circular convolution becomes pointwise multiplication in the frequency domain; short-time transforms give spectrograms.

title: Graphs, adjacency and degree matrices
description: Nodes and edges as matrices, paths via powers of the adjacency matrix, connected components.

title: Graph Laplacian and spectral clustering
description: L = D - A, the quadratic form sum of squared differences across edges, zero eigenvalues counting components, the Fiedler vector.

title: Random walks on graphs and PageRank
description: The row-normalised adjacency matrix, damping, and PageRank as the dominant eigenvector of the Google matrix.

title: Markov chains and transition matrices
description: The Markov property, row-stochastic matrices, n-step probabilities as matrix powers.

title: Stationary distributions, ergodicity and MCMC
description: The stationary distribution as a left eigenvector with eigenvalue 1, convergence for ergodic chains, detailed balance and the link to Metropolis-Hastings.

title: Definite integrals and the fundamental theorem of calculus
description: Area as a limit of sums, antiderivatives, substitution and integration by parts.

title: Expectations as integrals; the Gaussian integral
description: Densities integrate to one, E[g(x)] = integral g p, multiple integrals, and the value of the integral of exp(-x^2/2).

title: Numerical integration: trapezoid, Simpson, Monte Carlo
description: Quadrature rules with their error orders, and why Monte Carlo wins in high dimension.
